scope: Proposition 3.4 (Root-direction log-concavity) of the manuscript “An FPRAS for Common Integer Polymatroid Bases with Binary Capacities” (preprints/An-FPRAS-for-Common-Integer-Polymatroid-Bases-with-Binary-Capacities-October-5-2026/polymatroid-fpras.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 114 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 c14d087890444879), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 14. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let f1, f2 be integral normalized submodular functions on E, not necessarily nondecreasing, and define Y (d) = #{(x1, x2) ∈ (B(f1) ∩ ZE ) × (B(f2) ∩ ZE ) : x1 − x2 = d}. For d0 ∈ ZE and distinct j, k ∈ E, put y(t) = Y (d0 + t(ej − ek)), t ∈ Z. The positive support of y is an integer interval, possibly empty or a singleton. For integers a < t < b with y(a), y(b) > 0, y(t) ≥ y(a)(b−t)/(b−a) y(b)(t−a)/(b−a) . (3.10)
